Brown volleyball to host Cornell and Columbia in Ivy League matchups
Brown volleyball returns home for two key Ivy League matches against Cornell and Columbia this weekend. The Bears look to improve their conference standing after recent close losses.
The Brown volleyball team announced on Oct. 15 that it will return to the Pizzitola Sports Center this weekend for two Ivy League conference matches, facing Cornell on Friday at 6 p.m. and Columbia on Saturday at 5 p.m.
Brown enters the weekend with a record of 4-9 overall and 2-3 in Ivy League play, following a pair of five-set losses last weekend against Penn and Princeton. In the match against Penn, freshman Elle Holley led Brown with 15 kills on a .231 hitting percentage, while junior Fisayo Afonja contributed 14 kills. Junior Julia Kakkis recorded 42 assists, and freshman Sophie Haskell had 25 digs. Sophia Wolfson reached her milestone of 500 career kills during this game.
Against Princeton, Afonja again led the Bears with 17 kills, closely followed by Holley with 16. Kakkis posted another strong performance with 46 assists, and Haskell added 17 digs. The Bears currently stand sixth in the Ivy League standings.
Cornell comes into Friday's contest undefeated in Ivy League play at 5-0 and holds an overall record of 9-5. The Big Red are coming off consecutive three-set sweeps over Dartmouth and Harvard at home. Cornell maintains a team hitting percentage of .227; Ava Bogan leads the league individually with a .391 mark, while Bogan and Mackenzie Parsons have the top two points-per-set averages in the conference.
Columbia arrives for Saturday's matchup holding a conference record of 1-4 and an overall mark of 7-7. After losing to Harvard last Friday in three sets, Columbia secured its first Ivy win this season by defeating Dartmouth in five sets at home. The Lions post a team hitting percentage of .209 while allowing opponents .222; Elena Maynulet leads Columbia offensively with 142 kills, while Delaney Seaman leads defensively with 171 digs.
